reasons: Lake identity is verified and lists case_name United States v. Sokolow, court U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided 1989-04-03, and year 1989.
Lake citations list official cite 490 U.S. 1, vendor-neutral cite 1989 U.S. LEXIS 1694, and the same three parallel cites: 109 S. Ct. 1581, 104 L. Ed. 2d 1, and 57 U.S.L.W. 4401.

The opinion states: 'Any one of these factors is not by itself proof of any illegal conduct and is quite consistent with innocent travel. But we think taken together they amount to reasonable suspicion.'
The opinion also ties that point to reasonable suspicion generally, stating that lawful or innocent conduct can justify suspicion and that the principle applies to the reasonable-suspicion inquiry.
residual_risks: The proposition should remain framed as 'can' rather than 'always will'; the opinion is applying totality-of-the-circumstances reasoning.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If used outside this case page, tie the holding to Terry reasonable suspicion and totality of the circumstances.

reasons: The opinion says the decision turns on whether agents had reasonable suspicion and discusses the concept of reasonable suspicion as not reducible to a neat set of legal rules.

residual_risks: No separate home-page taxonomy defining the threshold for 'Key' was disclosed.

residual_risks: No separate home-page taxonomy defining the threshold for 'Key' was disclosed.
